name: Graphite Layered Hexagonal Lattice
semanticDescription: NCERT Class 10 Chemistry Ch 4 Fig 4.7(b) layered planar hexagonal carbon crystal lattice of graphite. Carbon atoms form 2D honeycomb sheets with sp2 hybridization, 120° bond angles, and 1.42 Å covalent bonds, separated by a 3.35 Å interlayer gap held by weak van der Waals forces. Dual presentation collections: 'Graphite_Lattice_Full' (3 stacked graphene sheets in ABAB stacking with vertical cyan van der Waals links on a dark studio slate plinth) and 'Graphite_Lattice_Detail' (exploded two-layer view demonstrating interlayer sliding shear vectors for solid lubricity, delocalized pi-electrons for high electrical conductivity, 120° trigonal planar angle arc, and educational property plaque).
simplifications: 3 stacked parallel graphene sheets demonstrate both in-plane hexagonal rings and interlayer spacing.
Interlayer van der Waals forces visualized with vertical cyan links.
Detail view includes layer sliding shear vectors, delocalized pi-electrons, and 120° angle arc.
